fixes.explanation: Egypt it is, friend. The writer says the LORD brought Israel out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt. (2 Kings 17:7) It's a reminder of what the LORD had already done for them. The writer starts here before listing everything they did.

Close, friend, but the text doesn't say that. Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, did evil in the sight of the LORD, “…but not like the kings of Israel who preceded him.” (2 Kings 17:2) So his evil wasn't like theirs. The text still calls it evil.

You got it, baker. Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, found out that Hoshea “…had not paid tribute to the king of Assyria as in previous years.” (2 Kings 17:4) Hoshea had also conspired to send envoys to King So of Egypt. That's like skipping your rent and then quietly sending a message to a different landlord.

Nice try, but the text shows no double bill. The king of Assyria discovered Hoshea's plan and the missing tribute, and he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. (2 Kings 17:4) Paying double isn't part of what the verse says.

Egypt is in the story, friend, but not like that. Hoshea had conspired to send envoys to King So of Egypt, and that's what Assyria found out about. The king of Assyria's answer was to arrest Hoshea and put him in prison. (2 Kings 17:4) The verse doesn't send Hoshea to Egypt.
Right on the money, baker. The king of Assyria marched up to Samaria and besieged it for three years. (2 Kings 17:5) That's three whole years.

No treaty in this story, friend. The king of Assyria invaded the whole land, marched up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years. (2 Kings 17:5) The verse mentions no deal, only a siege that lasted three years.

Samaria wasn't a rest stop, friend. The king of Assyria invaded the whole land, marched up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years. (2 Kings 17:5) Egypt had been part of Hoshea's plan, but this verse has the king of Assyria besieging Samaria, not passing it by.
That's the one, baker. In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria. (2 Kings 17:6) The siege that began in verse 5 led to this. Samaria was taken.

Hoshea had conspired to send envoys to King So of Egypt, so I see why you'd think it. But the text shows no rescue. In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria. (2 Kings 17:6) Help from Egypt never shows up in these verses.

The text doesn't give Samaria that ending, friend. After the three-year siege, the king of Assyria captured it in the ninth year of Hoshea. (2 Kings 17:6) Then he carried the Israelites away to Assyria.

You got it, baker. The Israelites “…set up for themselves sacred pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.” (2 Kings 17:10) Every high hill, every green tree. That's a lot of places, and the writer wants us to see how many.
That's the one, baker. They “…made for themselves two cast idols of calves and an Asherah pole.” (2 Kings 17:16) Two calves, plus the pole.
Dagon doesn't appear in this verse. The text says Israel “…made for themselves two cast idols of calves and an Asherah pole.” (2 Kings 17:16) It names two cast idols of calves, not a carved image.
Ephraim isn't the one here, friend. The verse says the LORD removed Israel from His presence and “Only the tribe of Judah remained…” (2 Kings 17:18) Judah fills the blank.
Dan isn't the one here, friend. The text says the LORD removed Israel from His presence, and “Only the tribe of Judah remained…” (2 Kings 17:18) So Judah is the answer. Dan isn't mentioned.

You got it, baker. The LORD removed Israel from His presence “…as He had declared through all His servants the prophets.” (2 Kings 17:23) So the word had come through the prophets. They had declared it ahead of time.
